name: Exposed services
summary: Ducts, pipes, stairs and cables stay in view on the outside or the ceiling, often colour-coded, so the building shows how it works.
how: Leave each duct, pipe and cable tray in view; paint them or leave them raw metal.
Give each system one colour: for example blue for air, green for water, yellow for electricity.
Keep the floor plate free; put the services on the facade or the ceiling.

origin.note: The Centre Pompidou of Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers puts its ducts, pipes and escalators on the outside.

adoptions.via: Loft conversions leave ducts, pipes and cable trays bare on the ceiling.

sources.title: Kenneth Powell, Richard Rogers: Complete Works (1999)
